intro: Custodial work builds reliability, time management and care with equipment and chemicals. The closest of the 25 careers below is Dishwashers at a 78% match, but Hazardous Materials Removal Workers are also 77% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $49,450, which is 34% more than janitors earn.
why_it_works: Keeping a building clean means planning routes, working alone and handling cleaning products safely. O*NET rates coordination and time management at 2.75 out of 5 for this job. Laundry, material moving and hazmat removal draw on the same habits. All 25 matches need no extra schooling, and most pay more than the $36,840 janitor median. The skills to build are running and monitoring equipment.
tips: Ask about building maintenance helper roles; they lead to repair work that pays more.
Tapers earn $68,270, which is 85% more, and train on the job in construction.
Hazmat training certificates are short and open better-paid removal jobs.

faq.q: What jobs can former janitors do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Dishwashers (78%), laundry and dry-cleaning workers (77%) and hand laborers and material movers (77%), based on O*NET 31.0. Material movers earn $40,240, which is 9% more than the $36,840 median for janitors and cleaners.

faq.q: Which careers for janitors pay more?
faq.a: 21 of the 25 matches pay more. Water vessel captains, mates and pilots earn $92,460 (151% more), railroad brake and signal operators $68,840 (87% more) and Tapers $68,270 (85% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Vessel roles need licensing and sea time first.

faq.q: Do janitors need more education to change jobs?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than janitors and cleaners already have. In the closest match, 56% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and most training happens in the first month on the job.

The skills that most often need work are operation and control, operations monitoring, quality control analysis and operations analysis. Social perceptiveness already rates 2.62 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so learning to run machines is the main step toward better pay.
